concepts.heading: Beyond the Binary
concepts.alt: A guide holding a friendly plush unicorn with small coloured dials floating around it
concepts.plain: Gender has several parts: who you are inside, how you show it, your body and who you like.

concepts.heading: Why the Binary Fails
concepts.alt: A guide stepping out of one of two boxes onto an open colourful floor
concepts.plain: Two boxes, man and woman, do not fit everyone.

concepts.heading: Intersex Realities
concepts.plain: Some people are born with bodies that are not clearly male or female.

concepts.heading: Gender Identity Is Self-Determined
concepts.alt: A guide holding a mirror and pointing proudly at herself, a small crown above
concepts.plain: Only you can say what your gender is.

options: No, even biological sex isn't binary
checks.explanation: No, even biological sex isn't binary. Even biological sex isn't binary. By one widely cited estimate, up to 1.7% of people are born with intersex variations — differences in chromosomes, hormones, or anatomy that don't fit typical male or female categories.

checks.prompt: Who is the ultimate authority on a person's gender identity?
checks.explanation: That person. The most important principle in understanding gender is that each person is the ultimate authority on their own gender identity.

1bc0af31-f1ac-4f55-a6c4-e6799069e3e4.takeaway: Gender has several parts, and each person is the expert on their own.

concepts.heading: Understanding Transgender Experience
concepts.alt: A guide smiling as he steps forward into a beam of light, an old photo frame behind him
concepts.plain: Transgender means your gender is different from what was written down at your birth.

concepts.heading: Nonbinary Identities
concepts.alt: A guide standing under a big umbrella with many small coloured shapes beneath it
concepts.plain: Nonbinary means your gender is not simply man or woman.

concepts.heading: The WPATH Standards of Care
concepts.alt: A guide holding a guidebook marked with a medical cross and a heart
concepts.plain: Doctors follow shared guidelines for giving trans people good care.

concepts.heading: Addressing Common Misconceptions
concepts.alt: A guide popping a dark thought bubble with a pin
concepts.plain: Many common beliefs about trans people are wrong, and they do harm.

options: An umbrella term for identities outside the man/woman binary
checks.explanation: An umbrella term for identities outside the man/woman binary. Nonbinary is an umbrella term for gender identities outside the man/woman binary.

checks.prompt: Is being trans a mental illness?
checks.explanation: No, it is not. The lesson names this as a harmful misconception: being trans is not a mental illness.

80a036e5-b135-48cc-a960-7935a07cadd0.takeaway: Trans and nonbinary people know who they are. Respect and good care help them thrive.

concepts.heading: Why Pronouns Matter
concepts.alt: Two guides greeting each other with a wave, each wearing a small name tag with a heart
concepts.plain: Using someone's right pronouns shows that you see them.

concepts.heading: Common Pronoun Sets
concepts.plain: Common sets are he, she and they. Some people use others.

concepts.heading: How to Ask About Pronouns
concepts.alt: A guide shaking hands while pointing to her own name tag first
concepts.plain: Share your own pronouns first, then ask for theirs.

concepts.heading: When You Make a Mistake
concepts.alt: A guide wincing with a hand raised, then smiling, a small plaster on a heart beside him
concepts.plain: If you get it wrong: say sorry briefly, correct it and move on.

concepts.heading: Pronouns and Consent
concepts.plain: Respecting pronouns is a form of consent. People decide how they are spoken about.

options: They are a basic part of how we acknowledge each other
checks.explanation: They are a basic part of how we acknowledge each other. Pronouns are a fundamental part of how we refer to and acknowledge each other.

checks.prompt: You use the wrong pronoun by accident. What does the lesson say first?
checks.explanation: Everyone makes pronoun mistakes sometimes. Everyone makes pronoun mistakes sometimes. What matters is how you handle it: 1.

0593fa05-660b-42b7-842c-1554966cf731.takeaway: Use the pronouns people ask for. If you slip, fix it quickly and move on.

concepts.heading: Beyond Tolerance to Genuine Support
concepts.alt: One climbs a ladder while the other two hold it steady
concepts.plain: Understanding is a start. Support means doing something.

concepts.heading: Being a Genuine Ally
concepts.alt: A guide rolling up his sleeves and carrying a stack of boxes to help
concepts.plain: An ally is known by what they keep doing, not by a label.

concepts.heading: Supporting Partners Through Gender Exploration
concepts.alt: Two guides walking side by side, she holds a lantern that lights the path for him
concepts.plain: If a partner explores their gender, you can feel a lot and still support them.

concepts.heading: Gender Diversity in Your Relationships and Communities
concepts.plain: Our communities can lead by making space for every gender.

concepts.heading: Curiosity vs. Fetishization
concepts.alt: A guide holding a magnifying glass in one hand and a heart in the other, choosing the heart
concepts.plain: Be interested in the person. Do not treat them as a category or a turn-on.

concepts.heading: When to Seek Support
concepts.plain: A gender-affirming therapist can help you or your partner.

checks.explanation: Consistent behaviour. Genuine allyship is not about identity or labels — it's about consistent behavior.

checks.prompt: When dating trans people, the lesson draws a line between genuine curiosity and…
checks.explanation: Fetishization. When dating or being intimate with trans people, there is an important distinction between genuine curiosity and fetishization.

e7c39870-32fc-4e07-8ffc-1f540f2dd2dc.takeaway: Real support is steady action, not just good intentions.
